claims.claim: A project-trust denial returned by reload's resolveProjectTrust callback was overwritten with approval, so the post-decision pass reloaded project resources.

The reload now applies the actual trust decision to the settings manager before the finalized settings reload, preserving bootstrap exclusion and post-decision phase separation for user/global, project, and CLI resources.
The standalone regression exercises the real DefaultResourceLoader reload lifecycle through .prale-eval/subject.mjs and asserts bootstrap exclusion, denial, approval, and follow-up reload behavior.

validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root with Node v24.14.0 (exit 0). The regression loads the real packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts through .prale-eval/subject.mjs and checks four behaviors. (1) During the bootstrap pass project extensions are absent while user/global and CLI extensions are present, and trust is disabled. (2) When resolveProjectTrust returns false, the post-reload extension set remains user+CLI only and the settings manager stays untrusted with the finalized settings reload observing false. (3) When resolveProjectTrust returns true, project extensions appear alongside user/global and CLI, and trust is recorded as true. (4) A follow-up reload with no trust decision after a denial does not revive project resources. I verified fault detection by temporarily restoring the original unconditional setProjectTrusted(true): the script failed at the denial assertion with actual ['cli','project','user'] versus expected ['cli','user'], then the fix was restored and the script passed again. The repository's vitest suites could not be run because no node_modules are installed and dependencies must not be installed; the standalone Node regression is the focused validation and needs no dependencies or network.
